title: Return of the Earlier Visit Fee on Recalls, Homeowner Service Contracts Cash Acceptances
content:
For the acceptance of a company-elected offer on a recall of earlier Bridgewell work under a Homeowner Service Contract, and only for such an acceptance, part or all of the standard visit fee paid for that earlier work is returned within the payment as described here, while fees are still not refunded because a failure is determined not covered or because the customer declines a covered repair or replacement; every other fee remains under the general service call fee rule.

**Visit-fee return.** The visit-fee return is the standard visit fee collected on the request of the earlier Bridgewell work that the recall names, multiplied by the return share and rounded to the cent. Accepting the cash closes the claim, so this credit, which Bridgewell owes on the request, is settled in the same payment: it is added to the accepted offer amount as a flat dollar amount, never compounded, before the total is compared with the remaining item and aggregate benefits.

| The accepted request | Return share |
|---|---|
| a recall that names an earlier Bridgewell replacement, whose installed unit has failed outright | 1.00 (the whole fee) |
| a recall that names an earlier Bridgewell repair | 0.50 (half the fee) |
| not a recall | nothing |

The earlier work is the authorization whose number the recall request carries; its own service request shows the standard visit fee that was collected.

*Hypothetical:* a recall names an earlier repair whose request was charged a 150.00 standard visit fee: the return is 75.00. Had it named an earlier replacement, the return would be 150.00.
